The ksz9477 DSA switch driver is currently updating some MMD registers
on the internal port PHYs to address some chip errata. However
errata are really a property of the PHY itself
part of
column2: so this is kind of a layering violation. It makes more sense for

column1: these writes to be done inside the driver which binds to the PHY and not
the driver for the containing device.
This also addresses some issues where the ordering of when these writes
are done may have been incorrect
column2: causing the link to erratically fail to

column1: come up at the proper speed or at all. Doing this in the PHY driver
during config_init ensures that they happen before anything else tries to
change the state of the PHY on the port.
The new code also ensures that autonegotiation is disabled during the
register writes and re-enabled afterwards
